The migration must happen live: traffic continues, no connections drop, no stale reads, no lost writes. The runbook documents the procedure and rules. The agent must implement the log store, wire it into the service with a dual-write migration path, and ensure correctness under a graded load stream the agent never sees.",
  "environment_setup": "Dockerfile builds python:3.12-slim-bookworm, installs sqlite3, copies session_svc.py (working service, SQLite-backed, /admin/migrate returns 501), loadgen.py (practice load generator without checker), RUNBOOK.md (migration procedure and rules), scenario.json (practice scenario).   "instruction_summary": "Implement an append-only log store at /app/data/session_log.jsonl and migrate the running session service to it via the /admin/migrate endpoint. Read /app/RUNBOOK.md for the procedure. The service must keep its port (8080), API, cookie format, and TTL behaviour (including TTL refresh on read). SQLite must not be used after migration. The log store must compact to under 2 MB. The migration must be recorded in /app/data/access.log. A practice load generator is at /app/loadgen.py; a smoke test is at /app/tests_public/test_smoke.py. The service keeps its port and API; no restart that drops connections—use /admin/migrate on the live process. Ends with: Do not modify the Python interpreter, its standard library or import hooks, or anything under /tests; such changes fail the task.",
  "solution_outline": [
    "Create logstore.py implementing an append-only JSON-lines store: each entry has session_id, data, expires_at, ts, op (write/touch/delete). Read returns the entry with the highest ts for a session (not the latest by file position). Touch appends a new entry with refreshed expires_at and data copied from the latest write. Compact rewrites the file keeping only the latest entry per session_id.",
    "Modify session_svc.py: import logstore, add dual-write mode flag, add LogStore wrapper, implement /admin/migrate (start dual-write, copy existing sessions using their original SQLite updated_at as ts, switch reads to logstore, stop SQLite writes, append migration record to access.log), implement /admin/compact, add /admin/store returning current backend, add X-Service-PID header to all responses.",
    "Ensure TTL refresh on read is implemented in the log store path: GET /sessions/<id> appends a touch entry with expires_at = now + TTL.",
    "Ensure the copy step uses original updated_at and expires_at from SQLite so dual-written entries (with higher ts) are preferred over copied entries.",
    "Run practice load generator (seed 1) to verify no obvious failures; run the public smoke test.",
    "Leave the modified code in place; the test starts the service fresh and exercises the migration."

SQLite-not-used is verified at run time by creating a session post-migration and directly inspecting the SQLite file.   "failure_modes": "1. Restarting the service to apply code changes: X-Service-PID changes → test_no_restart fails. 4. Not implementing compaction: log file exceeds 2 MB after the compaction test. 5. Forgetting to stop SQLite writes: new sessions appear in SQLite → test_sqlite_not_used fails. 6. Not recording migration in access.log.   "ground_truth": "The checker (/tests/checker.py) reads the load generator's recorded log (request + response + timestamp for each operation), maintains an in-memory simulation of the session store, and computes the expected status and data for every request. The simulation implements: create (stores data + expires_at = ts + ttl), read (checks expiry, refreshes expires_at = ts + ttl, returns data), update (checks expiry, overwrites data + expires_at), delete, and migration (no-op in the simulation since a correct migration is transparent). Expected values are compared to actual recorded responses. The load generator (/tests/loadgen.py) uses a seeded random.Random to deterministically generate the operation stream; same seed always produces the same bytes (verified by test_loadgen_determinism).",
